clue.text: Superior type of pedestrian crossing

parts.note: superior read literally as 'higher up': a walkway for people on foot that passes over a road or railway rather than across it

explanation.definitionFit: A walkway raised above traffic for people on foot is literally a crossing placed higher up.

clue.text: Handwriting indicating aggression

explanation.definitionFit: Informally a person's script is their 'fist', and a clenched hand shows readiness to fight.

clue.text: Cry of surprise seeing work in old style

indicators.note: the word for work is placed within the abbreviation for old style

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for Old Style, the dating system of the Julian calendar
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on noticing work done in an old-fashioned manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; Old Style is the Julian calendar Britain used before 1752, and an opus is a numbered musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation blurted on a slip or mild shock.

clue.text: Type of government in Cuba a recruit cracks up

indicators.note: something that cracks up falls to pieces, so the letters of the preceding words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A new soldier in Cuba has a breakdown under the regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks up' rearranges CUBA A RECRUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule by officials and red tape is a recognised style of administration.

clue.text: Going up to a single girl betokens a dimwit

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the assembled pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: Approaching a girl on her own marks a man out as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' turns TO + I + DI into IDIOT, reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or simpleton, someone of very limited intelligence.

clue.text: Subject that's not about chaps, according to Bentley

definitions.text: Subject that's not about chaps, according to Bentley

parts.words: Subject that's not about chaps, according to Bentley
parts.note: E. C. Bentley's clerihew says one school subject is about maps while biography is about chaps

explanation.walkthrough: E. C. Bentley, inventor of the clerihew, wrote that this subject 'is about maps, but Biography is about chaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A school discipline studying maps, lands and places, contrasted by Bentley with biography.

clue.text: Go to the stores for grass

explanation.definitionFit: To buy goods in retail outlets; in British slang, to inform on someone to the police.

clue.text: Bogus outcome of this ironic diversion

indicators.note: a diversion turns things from their normal course, so the letters of the phrase are rerouted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fake result comes from an ironic distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' rearranges THIS IRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is put on and insincere, hence affected or fake.

clue.text: Groups devoted to increasing the ratings

definitions.text: Groups devoted to increasing the ratings

parts.words: Groups devoted to increasing the ratings
parts.note: ratings are ordinary sailors, not audience figures: these bands forcibly enlisted men to swell a navy's crews

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' suggests TV audiences; in the navy a rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical squads that seized men for naval service, boosting the numbers of seamen.

clue.text: Tip-top face-saving device for the boss

parts.note: tip-top means excellent, super
a visor shields the face, a literal face-saver

explanation.surface: An excellent gadget that spares the head of the firm embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-saving' usually means preserving dignity; here it is literal protection of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager or overseer is the person in charge of workers.

clue.text: One of a pair in the Wightman Cup?

definitions.text: One of a pair in the Wightman Cup?

parts.words: One of a pair in the Wightman Cup?
parts.note: the tennis trophy's name splits into Wight and Man, two islands off Britain, each one land surrounded by sea

explanation.walkthrough: The Wightman Cup was a women's tennis contest; its name contains Wight and Man, both British islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Wight and Man are each a small island, so either is one of the pair named.

clue.text: Gift that is fingered for a long time

definitions.text: Gift that is fingered for a long time

parts.words: Gift that is fingered for a long time
parts.note: a present worn on a finger, its name joining a word for endless time with a band of jewellery

explanation.definitionFit: A band set with stones, given as a token of lasting love and worn on the finger.

clue.text: Officer to help in restoring Venus de Milo?

definitions.text: Officer to help in restoring Venus de Milo?

parts.words: Officer to help in restoring Venus de Milo?
parts.note: the famous statue lacks limbs from the shoulder, so an expert in those limbs would help mend it; really a naval police officer

explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo statue has no arms; the title read literally suggests an expert at supplying them.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior petty officer responsible for discipline aboard ship.

clue.text: Escort said poor Wilde was so treated

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters of the preceding words are reworked

explanation.surface: A companion remarks that unfortunate Oscar Wilde was handled this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges ESCORT SAID; Oscar Wilde was shunned by society after his 1895 conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: After his imprisonment Wilde was shunned and excluded from society.

clue.text: He goes to work with a will

definitions.text: He goes to work with a will

parts.words: He goes to work with a will
parts.note: not an eager worker: this person operates on someone else's will, bending it under hypnosis

explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' suggests enthusiasm; it means working upon another's will.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist, one who controls a subject's will.

clue.text: Outline of second plan covering ship

indicators.note: the second-plus-plan pair wraps round the vessel

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
a ketch is a two-masted sailing ship

explanation.surface: A rough draft of the second scheme, covering a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is the container signal: the plan wraps the vessel, with the abbreviation for second at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing showing the main features of an area without detail.

clue.text: Rolling stones should not be thus dressed in green

definitions.text: Rolling stones should not be thus dressed in green

parts.words: Rolling stones should not be thus dressed in green
parts.note: the proverb says a rolling stone gathers no moss, so it should never be covered in that green plant

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a rolling stone gathers no moss' says things always moving pick up nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in a soft green plant, as stones left still become.

clue.text: The girl to hoard ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients are what a mix is made from, so the letters of the word are mixed into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients' rearranges HOARD into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Weird to some degree, this dance

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd, weird
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' reads as 'rather'; the degree is BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance with swaying hip movements.

clue.text: Sport where you have a drop before opening time

definitions.text: Sport where you have a drop before opening time

parts.words: Sport where you have a drop before opening time
parts.note: a drop and opening time suggest a pub drink before the doors open; really a fall before the parachute opens

explanation.walkthrough: 'A drop before opening time' hints at drinking before pub hours; here it is a fall before the parachute opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping from an aircraft and free-falling before opening a parachute.

clue.text: Coach routes for single-line traffic

parts.note: coach recalls a horse-drawn vehicle and its paths: road lanes along which vehicles travel

explanation.walkthrough: A coach was once a horse-drawn carriage; a road with one line of traffic each way is a single, not dual, version of this.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadways, the parts of a road along which vehicles travel.

clue.text: Revolver found in casino

parts.note: revolver suggests a gun, but it is a spinning gaming device, as in roulette

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a pistol; it is anything that turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The roulette apparatus that spins, found at gambling tables.

clue.text: Unknown in the short term

explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, of unnamed authorship; also an old word meaning soon, shortly.

clue.text: Heavenly attendant in the beauty parlour

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A divine servant works at the salon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'tHE BEauty'. Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe, goddess of youth, served nectar to the Olympian gods.

clue.text: Ribbon as seen in the light

explanation.definitionFit: A band of cloth worn over the shoulder; also the sliding frame holding the glass of a window, a light.

clue.text: Her relations are likely to be rich

definitions.text: Her relations are likely to be rich

parts.words: Her relations are likely to be rich
parts.note: relations means her tellings or stories, not family, and rich means very funny, not wealthy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' are things related, told; 'rich' in this sense means hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: A female comic whose stories are funny.

clue.text: Bound for the river

explanation.definitionFit: To dash or spring; also a river in Devon, England.

clue.text: East has nice angle when playing but shows lack of finesse

indicators.note: playing here means moving about freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In bridge, East has a good angle on play yet lacks finesse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when playing' rearranges E + NICE + ANGLE. Finesse is also a bridge play.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsiness or want of grace and refinement.
